title: Gravity pulls objects toward Earth, so a dropped object is falling
summary: Gravity pulls objects toward Earth, so a dropped object is falling.
body: NASA Space Place says gravity is why a person lands after a jump, and why something comes down after it is dropped or thrown, instead of drifting off. The page calls Earth's gravity the pull that keeps a person on the ground and makes things come down. A separate NASA fact sheet lists an escape speed for leaving Earth; that line is a different claim and is not what this card says. The page's article date is 17 December 2020.

sources.title: What Is Gravity?
sources.author: NASA Space Place
sources.note: NASA Space Place, article last updated 17 December 2020. Paraphrase of the page's own sentence. Public-domain US federal page. Supports the sentences that things fall when dropped or thrown, and that Earth's gravity makes things fall.
